abstract_sentences.text: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) break the rigid left-to-right constraint of traditional LLMs, enabling token generation in arbitrary orders.

evidence.anchor: break the rigid left-to-right constraint

abstract_sentences.text: Intuitively, this flexibility implies a solution space that strictly supersets the fixed autoregressive trajectory, theoretically unlocking superior reasoning potential.

evidence.anchor: solution space that strictly supersets the fixed autoregressive trajectory

abstract_sentences.text: However, in this paper, we find that for general reasoning tasks (e.g., mathematics and coding), arbitrary order generation may in fact limit the reasoning potential of dLLMs.

evidence.anchor: arbitrary order generation may in fact limit the reasoning potential

abstract_sentences.text: We observe that dLLMs tend to exploit this order flexibility to bypass high-uncertainty tokens that are crucial for exploration, which can lead to a premature collapse of solution coverage.

evidence.anchor: bypass high-uncertainty tokens

abstract_sentences.text: This observation motivates a rethink of RL approaches for dLLMs, where considerable complexities, such as handling combinatorial trajectories and intractable likelihoods, are often devoted to preserving this flexibility.

evidence.anchor: combinatorial trajectories and intractable likelihoods

abstract_sentences.text: We show that effective reasoning can be elicited by simply forgoing arbitrary order and applying standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) instead.

evidence.anchor: forgoing arbitrary order and applying standard Group Relative Policy Optimization

abstract_sentences.text: Our approach, JustGRPO, is minimalist yet surprisingly effective (e.g., 89.1% accuracy on GSM8K) while fully retaining the parallel decoding ability of dLLMs.

evidence.anchor: 89.1% accuracy on GSM8K

final_judgment.single_storyline: dLLM arbitrary-order flexibility bypasses high-entropy logical forks and narrows practical coverage; AR training restores exploration and exact GRPO while inference remains parallel (pp. 4–10, Figs. 3–9, Eqs. 5–8).
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps AO/AR definitions, Pass@k/coverage, entropy mechanism, trajectory-likelihood tax, JustGRPO factorization, matched benchmark results, parallel decoding, and efficiency (pp. 4–10).
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–E move hyperparameters/rewards, temperature and sampler robustness, extended entropy, random-order failures, general capability, and bidirectional-refinement boundary (pp. 15–19).
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest pattern is the evidence ladder Figure 3→4→5→6→7, followed by matched Table 2 and parallel-decoding Figure 8; Eqs. 5–7 make the exact surrogate concrete (pp. 4–9).
final_judgment.largest_gap: Entropy degradation is observational rather than intervention-based; one RL base model, heterogeneous first-pass baselines, and no uncertainty reporting further limit generality (pp. 6, 8–10, 15–19).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Before treating order flexibility as an advantage, test high-k coverage and fork-local entropy, then separately verify training-time exploration and inference-time parallel execution (pp. 4–7, 9–10).
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule is supported for the tested math/code tasks, dLLMs, and confidence/semi-AR/random settings; it is not a theorem for all tasks, samplers, models, or bidirectional refinement (pp. 1, 4–5, 17–19).
